findings.message: This race test never forces the interleaving that the round-3 fix guards, so it can pass with `if (r.status === "completed") continue;` (release-tracking.ts:92) deleted. The fix only matters when this exact order happens: recordDeployment holds the release row lock (releaseOf `for update`, services.ts:67), completeReached's plain select (release-tracking.ts:87) still sees the release as open, and recordDeployment commits before `tracked()` takes the lock. In every other order the status predicate on the select already skips the row. Firing two promises 5 times makes that window a matter of chance. `Promise.allSettled` also discards rejections: if either service throws (lock timeout, an error from the change), the test still checks only that there is one completion and passes. Fix: make the interleaving deterministic. Open a transaction with the owner connection that locks the release `for update`, start upsertEnvironment, wait until it is blocked on that lock (poll `pg_locks`/`pg_stat_activity`), then complete the release through a Prod deployment in that held session, commit, and let the upsert finish. Assert that both calls fulfilled, and that `out.completed` is empty for that release.
findings.scenario: Revert line 92 → run the test → recordDeployment(Prod) commits before upsertEnvironment's select at release-tracking.ts:87, the select filters the row out, all 5 iterations pass. The test is green without the fix.

findings.message: This is an instance fix for the attribution finding. The upsert's audit now names the completed releases, but the other copies of the same fact still say a deployment caused the completion. completeReached still calls `completeBy(..., "deployment", by)`. So the `delivery.release_status_history` row (returned by get_release_history as `statusHistory`) and the `releaseStatusChanged` event payload (`source`, read by notifications) record `source: deployment` for a completion that an environment change caused. The finding asked for a history source or reason that shows the environment change. Fix: add a source for this case to `Source`, e.g. `"environment"` (with the DB check/enum and statusLabel/why text), and pass it here. Test that the QA-made-Prod history row and the event carry it.
findings.scenario: Release p1 (category prod) is deployed to QA. upsert_environment {name: QA, isProd: true} completes it. get_release_history shows the completion as `source: deployment` with QA's old deployment id, and the release-status-changed event also says `source: "deployment"`. No deployment was recorded at that time.

findings.message: `upsertEnvironment` now completes releases (it writes status, completed_at, completed_day, completion and completing_deployment_id on `delivery.release`), but the service's audit row only covers the environment: `resourceId` is the environment's id and `after` is the raw input. Nothing in the audit names the releases this call completed. The status-history row says `source: 'deployment'`, which hides that an environment change caused the completion. `updateRelease` puts the new status in its audited `after`. Fix: return the ids and versions of the completed releases from `completeReached` and include them in the upsert's audited `after` (for example `after: { ...input, completed: [...] }`). Use a history source or reason that shows an environment change caused the completion.
findings.scenario: An Admin marks QA as Prod and open release p1 (already deployed to QA) completes. The audit event for delivery.environment shows only {projectKey, name:'QA', isProd:true}. No audit record anywhere says p1 changed, and its history row reads 'completed by deployment, by Admin'.
